subject: Lognormal with additive effects on the original scale

messages.author: 5feb68cbfe09079c
messages.subject: Lognormal with additive effects on the original scale
parts:
I'd like to fit a model that assumes a lognormal distribution.  However, when I specify `family=lognormal()`, I get additive effects on the log scale (which is the reasonable thing in most cases) but I need additive effects on the original scale (which in my case happens to be milliseconds).  Is there a way to achieve this with brms?  For context, see here: http://discourse.mc-stan.org/t/lognormal-with-additive-effects-on-the-original-scale/1776

Thank you,

  Titus

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Lognormal with additive effects on the original scale
parts:
You want to do something like

y ~ lognormal(log(mu + X * a), sigma)

right? You can do this in brms using its non-linear syntax:

fit <- brm(bf(y ~ log(eta), eta ~ <predictors>, nl = TRUE),
           data = <data>, family = lognormal(),
           prior = prior(normal(0, 100), nlpar = eta))

However, I am not sure, if I want to recommend this model. Especially, you need "eta" to be positive, which is not trivial to achieve depending on your predictors.

Perhaps you could try the skew_normal() or exgaussian() families to deal with right-skewed data but handle predictors on the original scale.
